text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Thursday.

- Croatian Privatisation Fund is to announce a list of state assets for distribution among some 350,000 war invalids, refugees, families of the missing and ex-prisoners. Free vouchers will be worth some 8.5 billion kuna.
- State oil company INA accused Slovenia of limiting its operations in the neighbouring republic and said Croatia should take tit-for-tat measures against Slovenian firms.
- The government to announce whether it will exempt glucose syrup from the recently imposed ban on sugar imports, following the pressure by confectioners.
- Average monthly net salary was 2,137 kuna from October to December 1996, up 3.7 percent from the previous quarter.
- The Croatian embassy in Sarajevo protested to the Bosnian Foreign Ministry against what it described as a continuing "anti-Croatian campaign" in the Sarajevo press.

- Croatia is to invest 400 million kuna by the year 2000 in the construction of a water supply system in the country's eastern provinces. The project is one of the largest in infrastructure so far, says Reconstruction Minister Jure Radic.
- Croatia Airlines passangers can fly to New York via London and back for only $499, owing to a special prorate deal the carrier reached with Britain's Virgin Atlantic Airways.

- "I am leaving this summer but not because of any arms," says U.S. ambassador to Croatia Peter Galbraith after some U.S. media reported on his stepping down because of involvement in the shipment of Iranian arms to Bosnia via Croatia.

- Tokyo's Nozaki&Co Ltd firm will acquire a 60 percent stake in a future Zirje-tuna fishery, which will produce 30 to 40 tonnes of tuna a year for the Japanese market. Another 40 percent will be controlled by Conex Trade from Split.
- State oil firm INA hopes to secure a $100 million foreign syndicated loan. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
